# Analytical Solution for American Call Option Pricing

## Key Theorem: Early Exercise of American Calls

> **On a non-dividend paying stock, it is NEVER optimal to exercise an American call early.**

Therefore, for a **non-dividend paying stock**:

$$\boxed{C_{American} = C_{European} = BS(S, K, T, r, \sigma)}$$

---

## Black-Scholes Formula (Closed-Form Solution)

$$C = S_0 \, N(d_1) - K e^{-rT} N(d_2)$$

Where:

$$d_1 = \frac{\ln(S_0/K) + (r + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2)T}{\sigma\sqrt{T}}$$

$$d_2 = d_1 - \sigma\sqrt{T} = \frac{\ln(S_0/K) + (r - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2)T}{\sigma\sqrt{T}}$$

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| $S_0$ | Current stock price |
| $K$ | Strike price |
| $T$ | Time to maturity |
| $r$ | Risk-free rate (continuous) |
| $\sigma$ | Volatility of underlying |
| $N(\cdot)$ | Standard normal CDF |

---

## Proof: Why Early Exercise is Suboptimal

**Lower bound for European call:**

$$C_E \geq S_0 - Ke^{-rT}$$

**Immediate exercise payoff:**

$$C_{exercise} = S_0 - K$$

**Comparison:**

$$S_0 - Ke^{-rT} > S_0 - K \quad \text{since} \quad Ke^{-rT} < K$$

Therefore:

$$C_E \geq S_0 - Ke^{-rT} > S_0 - K$$

$$\Rightarrow \quad C_{American} = C_{European}$$

> 💡 **Intuition:** The time value of money makes it always better to *sell* the option rather than *exercise* it early.

---

## Case with Continuous Dividends

When the stock pays a **continuous dividend yield $q$**, early exercise *may* be optimal.

The European call (Merton model) gives a **lower bound**:

$$C = S_0 e^{-qT} N(d_1) - K e^{-rT} N(d_2)$$

$$d_1 = \frac{\ln(S_0/K) + (r - q + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2)T}{\sigma\sqrt{T}}, \qquad d_2 = d_1 - \sigma\sqrt{T}$$

---

## American Call with Dividends: Analytical Approximations

### 1. Roll-Geske-Whaley (Discrete Dividends)

For a single discrete dividend $D$ at time $t_d < T$:

$$C_A = (S_0 - De^{-rt_d})\,N(b_1) - (K - D)\,e^{-rT}N(b_2)$$
$$+ \;(S_0 - De^{-rt_d})\,M(a_1, -b_1;\,-\sqrt{t_d/T})$$
$$- \;Ke^{-rT}\,M(a_2, -b_2;\,-\sqrt{t_d/T})$$

where $M(\cdot,\cdot;\rho)$ is the **bivariate normal CDF**.

---

### 2. Barone-Adesi & Whaley (BAW) Quadratic Approximation

Split the price into European + early exercise premium:

$$C_A(S) = C_E(S) + A_2 \left(\frac{S}{S^*}\right)^{q_2}$$

**Critical price** $S^*$ satisfies:

$$S^* - K = C_E(S^*) + \left[1 - e^{-qT}N(d_1(S^*))\right]\frac{S^*}{q_2}$$

**Coefficients:**

$$q_2 = \frac{-(N-1) + \sqrt{(N-1)^2 + 4M/K}}{2}$$

$$A_2 = \frac{S^*}{q_2}\left[1 - e^{-qT}N(d_1(S^*))\right]$$

$$M = \frac{2r}{\sigma^2}, \quad N = \frac{2(r-q)}{\sigma^2}, \quad K = 1 - e^{-rT}$$

**Final formula:**

$$C_A = \begin{cases} C_E(S) + A_2\left(\dfrac{S}{S^*}\right)^{q_2} & \text{if } S < S^* \\[8pt] S - K & \text{if } S \geq S^* \end{cases}$$

---

## Summary Table

| Case | Analytical Solution Available? | Formula |
|------|-------------------------------|---------|
| No dividends | ✅ Exact | Black-Scholes |
| Continuous dividends | ⚠️ Approximate | BAW / Merton bound |
| Discrete dividends | ⚠️ Approximate | Roll-Geske-Whaley |
| General case | ❌ No closed form | Numerical methods (binomial, FD, MC) |

---

## Key Takeaway

$$\boxed{C_{American}^{\text{no dividend}} = S_0 N(d_1) - Ke^{-rT}N(d_2)}$$

The **exact** analytical solution exists only for the no-dividend case, where the American call equals the European Black-Scholes price.
